question: Does the site's hipfire sensitivity formula (degrees per count = sensitivity x 0.0017362342283 + 0.002314981532) reproduce the distances the game's own panel 'Mouse movement distances for 360 degree rotation' prints for Infantry Mouse Aim Sensitivity?

sourceFacts.source: In-game Settings > Infantry > Infantry Mouse Aim Sensitivity, panel text "Mouse movement distances for 360 degree rotation"
sourceFacts.unit: mouse travel for one full hipfire turn, as the panel prints it (one decimal)

siteCheckAsRecordedInFile.formula: degrees per count = sensitivity x 0.0017362342283 + 0.002314981532; cm/360 = 360 / (degrees per count x DPI) x 2.54
siteCheckAsRecordedInFile.result: all nine distances reproduce to the panel's displayed decimal (largest difference 0.045 cm at sensitivity 15 / 1,600 DPI and 55 / 1,600 DPI)
siteCheckAsRecordedInFile.test: scripts/live-fire.test.mjs, 'hipfire cm/360 reproduces the in-game settings panel distances'

recomputedByThisDraft.method: python mousecheck.py (cwd = the L4063 run folder; reads the JSON file, applies the file's formula: cm/360 = 360 / (degrees per count x DPI) x 2.54, inches = cm / 2.54)
recomputedByThisDraft.result: all nine distances round to the displayed one-decimal value in both cm and inches; the largest cm difference is 0.047 (sensitivity 15 at 1,600 DPI) and 0.043 (sensitivity 55 at 1,600 DPI) against the file's stated 'largest difference 0.045 cm', a rounding-level difference in the recorded figure

sourceFacts.note: The constant was first taken from the KovaaK's sensitivity converter's Battlefield 6 entry (read 21 October 2026); this panel is the game's own statement of the same conversion. The ADS scaling rule (Uniform Infantry Aiming coefficient) is not covered by the panel and stays a community formula.

inference: The panel is the game's own statement of the hipfire turn distance; the formula reproduces it at three sensitivities (15, 24, 55) and three DPI values (800, 1,600, 3,200), which pins the hipfire degrees-per-count constant. The ADS scaling rule is not covered.
